references.text: Abraham said about his wife Sarah, "She is my sister." So Abimelek, king of Gerar, took her.
Abraham answered, "I thought there was surely no fear of God in this place, and they would kill me because of my wife."

When the men of the place asked him about his wife, he said, "She is my sister." For he feared to say she was his wife, thinking, "otherwise the men of the place will kill me for Rebekah's sake, since she is beautiful to look at."
He allowed no one to oppress them; he rebuked kings on their behalf: "Do not touch my anointed ones; do my prophets no harm."
Abraham's fear of being killed in Egypt (12:12) is confirmed and resolved in a parallel event in Gerar (20:7), where his role as prophet becomes clear.
Direct narrative connection: The fear expressed in 12:12 is addressed and resolved in 12:19 within the same event.
